transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
U.S. envoy Steve Whitcoff and Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky
in Dublin on Thursday.
The meeting followed talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the discussions are the latest push to end the war in Ukraine.
Speaking on the airport tarmac, Kushner said Europe would henceforth take part in the talks.
"We cannot conclude this deal that the Europeans being at the table, we've been telling President
Putin that we believe that's very important."
But Putin has backed off none of his hard-line positions and said any peacekeeping force
in Ukraine would be a legitimate target.
Zelensky spoke earlier about the star-shield satellite connection being slowed down again.
He called it vital to intercepting Russia's new jet-powered drones.
"Because of the speed restrictions, we simply cannot catch up with them in time.
And this means more Russian strikes get through and more of our civilians are killed."
Ukraine is participating in the talks, but does not believe Putin wants to stop the war.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, TV.
The Trump administration is facing questions about its handling of the scandals surrounding
tech company Nvidia.
Former CEO Jensen Huang has maintained close ties to the president, raising questions about
what officials knew about his affair with a suspected Chinese spy and when.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reports.
Lawmakers from both parties say they want more information from Commerce Secretary Howard
Lutnick.
Commerce handles imports and exports, and so some lawmakers have questions about when
he knew Huang was in contact with a suspected Chinese asset, and whether the U.S. should
have tightened export controls on advanced chips.
On Thursday, South Carolina Republican Senator Tim Scott, chair of the Banking Committee,
said he's summoning Huang and Lutnick to hearings in early December.
Trump was also asked this week about what he knew and when.
He said he didn't recall receiving a memo with information about Huang's relationship.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
After a close election, Democrats will hold on to the governor's office in Kansas.
State Senator Cindy Holcher's win extends Democratic victories following the midterms.
Zach Boblett reports.
Despite Kansas having 400,000 more registered Republicans than Democrats, voters decided
to keep a Democrat in the governor's office.
Holcher will replace fellow Democrat Laura Kelly, who leaves office in January after
two terms.
Holcher ran a populist campaign focused on funding special education, property tax relief,
and a data center moratorium.
She beat a Republican backed early by President Trump.
The Kansas legislature is controlled by Republicans, but they lost seats in the midterms, which
will make it easier for Holcher to veto bills.
For NPR News, I'm Zach Boblett in Topeka.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Microsoft says service is improving across North America and much of Europe following
a massive outage on Thursday.
The company is also reporting signs of recovery in the Asia-Pacific region, though some users
are still facing access problems and email delays.
Crews are working to restore remaining services and clearing a backlog of messages.
Microsoft says it's not found evidence of malicious activity linked to the disruption.
The Kennedy Center says it's planning to shift its event ticketing to Ticketmaster.
An NPR investigation found the center's former president, Richard Grinnell, was a paid board
member of Ticketmaster's parent company at the time of the negotiations.
NPR's Anastasia Silukas reports.
Richard Grinnell was appointed as the Kennedy Center's president in February 2025, just
as President Trump became the institution's chairman.
A few months later, Grinnell was appointed to the board of Ticketmaster's parent company
Live Nation, for which he was paid over $260,000.
Critics say this raises conflict of interest concerns.
Both Ticketmaster and the Kennedy Center say their discussions predated Grinnell's dual
appointments, but current and former senior Kennedy Center staffers, who asked for anonymity
due to fears of retribution, say Ticketmaster was never under serious consideration by senior
staff until Grinnell's tenure.
The Kennedy Center's main theaters remain closed.
The annual Kennedy Center honors are scheduled to take place December 7 at Washington's Capital
One Arena, Anastasia Silukas, NPR News.
I'm Windsor Johnston, NPR News, in Washington.

Zelensky says slowed Starshield satellite connection lets Russian jet-powered drones get through
